headline: Ellison offers $40 billion to beef up Paramount's Warner Bros bid
summary: STORY: :: Oracle HandoutBillionaire Larry Ellison has thrown his weight behind the latest effort by Paramount Skydance to buy Warner Bros Discovery... ratcheting up the industry’s most closely watched takeover battle.The Oracle cofounder and father of Paramount Skydance CEO David Ellison on Monday said he will personally guarantee more than $40 billion for the deal...in an effort to pry Warner Bros Discovery away from selling its prized assets to rival bidder Netflix.The guarantee, disclosed in a Monday filing, sent shares of Paramount soaring as much as 8% in morning trading.It comes after Warner Bros last week asked its shareholders to reject Paramount’s more than $108 billion offer for the company, including its cable TV assets.The bid had raised doubts over its financing and the lack of a full guarantee from the Ellison family.Paramount said the amended terms do not change its $30-per-share all-cash offer for Warner Bros.It also agreed to raise the fee it would pay if the deal was blocked by regulators from $5 billion to $5.8 billion, matching Netflix's offer.Meanwhile, lawmakers from both parties have voiced concerns about consolidation in the media industry.A Paramount-Warner Bros merger would create a studio larger than industry leader Disney and combine two major television operators, a move some Democratic senators say would give one company control over "almost everything Americans watch on TV."A Netflix-Warner Bros tie-up would cement Netflix's dominance in streaming, creating a company with a combined 428 million subscribers.
